name: Preference and Naturalness of Scenes
description: Rebuilt from the published description of Kardan, Demiralp, Hout, Hunter, Karimi, Hanayik, Yourganov, Jonides & Berman (2015). Participants rate the same scenes twice on a 1–7 scale: how much they like each scene (shown for one second, then hidden) and how natural or man-made it is (the scene stays on screen). Task order is counterbalanced and the second task is not announced before the first ends, as in the paper. Response times are recorded from scene onset; the paper related them to naturalness. Differences from the original study: (1) The paper ran in PsychoPy in a lab and every participant rated all 307 scenes; here each participant rates 40 of the 307 scenes drawn at random, online. (2) The paper allowed up to 4 s for a preference rating; here there is no time limit. (3) Gender and age questions are additions. Bundled images are all 307 scenes released with Berman et al. (2014, PLOS ONE, CC BY), the paper's own stimulus set.
author: Kardan, Demiralp, Hout, Hunter, Karimi, Hanayik, Yourganov, Jonides & Berman
